en.commentary: Biotin deserves a direct comment because it dominates this category's marketing and the evidence behind it is narrower than the packaging suggests. Biotin supplementation reliably helps people with a genuine biotin deficiency, which is uncommon in anyone eating a normal diet. For everyone else the effect on hair and nails is modest at best. There is also a practical problem worth knowing: high-dose biotin interferes with several common laboratory assays including thyroid and cardiac markers, producing results that can look alarming or falsely reassuring. Tell your doctor if you take it, and stop several days before blood work. Where the evidence is stronger is in multi-ingredient formulations addressing the actual drivers of hair thinning, including nutrient status, stress, and hormonal factors. The Nutrafol Core for Women holds first at 9.4 because it has the most substantial clinical documentation in this category and its formulation targets several pathways at once. HUM Hair Sweet Hair at 8.9 and Vital Proteins Collagen Beauty at 8.9 are reasonable alternatives with clearer labelling. Give any of these six months before judging, since the hair growth cycle makes shorter assessments meaningless.
